name: What should I ask a contractor before starting a kitchen addition?

mainEntity.name: What should I ask a contractor before starting a kitchen addition?
mainEntity.text: What should I ask a contractor before starting a kitchen addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before starting a kitchen addition, homeowners should ask a contractor about experience with similar additions, permit handling, structural coordination, budget allowances, scheduling, and change-order procedures. It is especially important to know who will manage drawings, engineering, and inspections, because kitchen additions are more complex than surface-level remodels. Ask how the contractor handles hidden conditions, what items are included in the estimate, and which finishes are only allowances. Lead times for cabinets, tile, appliances, and fixtures should also be addressed early so the project schedule is realistic. Homeowners should also confirm jobsite protection, dust control, and whether temporary kitchen arrangements are part of the plan. A good contractor should be able to explain the sequence from design through final inspection in plain language. This is an underserved question because many people focus on price alone, when the real risk is unclear scope. The best content would function like a pre-construction checklist and help users compare contractors more intelligently.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask about permits, structural engineering, timeline, budget allowances, material lead times, and how change orders are handled. Also ask whether the contractor has experience with additions, not just cosmetic remodels. The answers should show how they manage complexity, inspections, and unexpected site conditions.
